messages:
maya: Quick Q — we're finalizing the public surface for insights-service. Browser/third-party clients want plain JSON. Internally we prefer gRPC + proto types. Options: (A) expose REST + maintain two stacks, (B) gRPC-only with a lightweight transcode proxy per region, (C) keep both and let callers choose. Thoughts on latency, quotas, telemetry, and rollout UX?

shawn: I lean (B). Single canonical server implementation (gRPC) + tiny transcode gateway keeps server codebase clean. We can use Envoy's gRPC-JSON transcoder or a tiny Node lambda. Latency hit is small if we colocate the proxy.

eli: +1 to single implementation for correctness, but major caveat: telemetry and quota mapping. If gateway rewrites requests, we need to carry original identity headers through so console shows the right route and org. Otherwise per-route token billing/quotas will be wrong.

carla: From product/console POV: we need per-route token/req breakdown and canary rollout signals visible in Dashboard. If we transcode, can we still show both "public route" and "service method" metrics in the UI?

shawn: Yes, but it requires that the gateway emits both sets of tags. Plan: gateway attaches x-original-route and proto_method tags to traces/metrics. Example (pseudo):

```
span.tags({
  "route_id": "public:/v1/insights",
  "proto_method": "insights.Insights/Get",
  "consumer_org": "org_123",
})
```

Also forward x-api-key, x-request-id to backend.

maya: What about error mapping? gRPC has rich status codes + details; HTTP clients expect HTTP codes and JSON error bodies. We need a consistent mapping so SDKs and the console can surface regressions.

eli: Agreed. We should define a canonical mapping doc. e.g. gRPC NOT_FOUND -> 404 with body {"code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "..."}. Also pass a structured error-detail header for tracing.

carla: Rollout UX: can we do a canary by route in Dedicated and Hosted? I want a 10% canary for new proto schema first for internal apps, then 1% for public endpoints. Dashboard should show canary traffic split and error deltas.

shawn: Technically doable via our routing policies. We can route a percentage to new variant (proto v2) at the gateway layer. For hosted we already have percentage routing in the control plane. Need two things: (1) route-level quotas counted by consumer and variant, (2) dashboard slices for variant.

maya: Quotas — where should rate-limits live? At gateway or at service? If gateway enforces quota, backend still needs to be hardened in case of bypass. Thoughts?

eli: Enforce at gateway for immediate rejection and better tail latency. Also keep conservative server-side checks as fail-safe. For billing/console accuracy, gateway should emit an authoritative usage event to our telemetry pipeline before responding 429.

shawn: Implementation risk: Envoy transcoder is mature but limited on streaming; if we need bidi or server streaming later we'd have to special-case. For now Insights is unary RPCs so ok. If we expect streaming features later, better to run a bespoke proxy that can fall back to proxying raw HTTP for streams.

carla: SDK/clients: We need clear guidance in README and codegen. If public surface is JSON, generate SDKs from OpenAPI (derived from proto). Dev experience is critical.

maya: Actionable proposal: 1) canonical server = gRPC (proto-first). 2) deploy per-region transcode gateway that preserves identity headers and emits both route+method telemetry tags. 3) gateway enforces quotas and emits usage events; backend keeps defensive checks. 4) console changes: show variant-level metrics + canary split + error mapping. 5) create short doc for error mapping and migration steps.

eli: +1 to proposal. I'll sketch the telemetry tag list and required headers.

shawn: I'll prototype an Envoy transcode config and a tiny express fallback for streaming cases. Will post in this thread when done. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary route "insights-v2-transcode" deployed to staging in us-west-2 at 2796012500.

maya: Nice. Please include a small integration test that asserts header propagation and that telemetry shows both tags.

carla: Also document the console changes we need for per-variant quotas and the canary widget. I'll file a design ticket after lunch.

shawn: Quick note — proto evolution: make all fields optional or use wrapper types where possible to avoid breaking public clients. We'll express deprecation in proto comments and version docs.

eli: One more: audit logs. Gateway must log original request payload hash and auth context for compliance.

maya: Sounds like we're aligned. If nobody objects, we'll cut an RFC/implementation plan and schedule a short design sync.

carla: No objections from me. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
